statements.text: Let $ $ be a datalog program and let $q( t)$ be an atom that may contain variables . Then a generalized proof tree of $q( t)$ w.r.t.\ program $ $ is defined as follows: Base case. If $q$ is an EDB predicate, then the tree consisting of a single node with label $q( t)$ is a generalized proof tree of $q( t)$. Inductive case. If $q$ is an IDB predicate, then a generalized proof tree $ T $ of $q( t)$ is of the following form: there exists a rule $R$ of the form $q( u) p_1( u_1) , p_μ( u_μ)$ and a substitution $σ$, such that the following conditions hold: [leftmargin=*] ; $q( t) = q(σ( u))$; ; for every $i \ 1, , μ\ $, there exists a proof tree $ T _i$ of $p_i(σ( u_i))$; ; $ T $ has a new root node $r$ labeled with $q( t)$ and the child nodes of $r$ are obtained by turning $ T _1, , T _μ$ into subtrees of $ T $, such that the root nodes of $ T _1, , T _μ$ become the child nodes of~$r$; ; the edges from the root to its child nodes are labeled with the rule~$R$.

A membership checking function is a function $h$ which takes as input an EDB-bounded rule $R$ with head predicate $q_ $, and a datalog program $ $, and outputs either true or false. In this work, we consider two membership checking functions: [leftmargin=*] ; $h_ eq $: A function that returns true if there exists some $R' $ that is identical to $R$, up to variable renaming, and false otherwise. Except for the discussion in sec:boundedness , this function is used throughout the remainder of the paper for deriving size bounds. ; $h_ cont $: A function that returns true if either (1) $q_ $ is not recursive in $ $ and there exists a predicate $q_ ' $ such that $ '$ subsumes $ $, or (2) there exists some $R' $ that is identical to $R$ up to variable renaming. Otherwise, it returns false. This function will be used in sec:boundedness in the semi-decision procedure for boundedness.

statements.text: A minimal adornment is an adornment in which every variable $v$ in the head of the rule appears in exactly one atom of the body of the adornment. No atom in the adornment consists solely of underscores. A minimal EDB-bounded datalog program $ ''$ is an EDB-bounded datalog program for which every rule has a minimal adornment.

The Stirling partition number , or Stirling number of the second kind , denoted by $S(n, k)$, counts the number of ways to partition a set of $n$ labeled elements into $k$ non-empty, unlabeled sets. It can be calculated by $S(n, k) = 1 k! Σ_ i = 0 ^k (-1)^ k - i k i i^n,$ based on the inclusion-exclusion principle.

A propositional Horn program $Σ$ is a set of rules of the form: $$p_0 p_1 p_2 p_n$$ where $p_0, p_1, p_n$ are Boolean variables. The program $Σ$ is equivalent to a datalog program $ $ if and only if there is a one-to-one mapping between all the derived ground atoms of $ $ and the minimal model of $Σ$.

proofs.text: The datalog program $ $ is analyzed via its EDB-bounded version, $ '$, by transforming it into an equivalent propositional Horn clauses. The clauses can be generated by choosing grounding for the head adornment. Since all adornments can be covered by one of its subsets of size at most $ ( )$, there are only $N^ ( ) $ possible groundings per rule. There are $| '|$ rules in the program, leading to at most $| '|· N^ ( ) $ Horn clauses. Let $k$ be the maximum number of atoms within a rule. The set of Horn clauses contains at most $(k+1)· f( )· N^ ( ) $ symbols. Solving a set of Horn clauses can be done in time linear to the number of symbols~ [cite] . Thus the overall running time is bounded by $O(| '|· N^ ( ) )$. Since $| '| ≤ f( ) · | |$ by thm:minimal-bound , the running time is bounded by $O(f( ) · | | · N^ ( ) )$.

It has been shown in Lemma~ [ref] that, apart from redundancy elimination, the body atoms of $ $ are precisely the atoms at the leaf nodes of a generalized proof tree $ T $ of $q_ ( t)$. Clearly the replacement of variables outside $ ( t)$ can be ignored since these variables never contribute to an edge cover. It only remains to show that an atom $A$ deleted as part of the redundancy elimination can never lead to a smaller edge cover of $q_ ( t)$. Indeed, suppose that $A$ is part of a cardinality-minimum edge cover of $ ( t)$ from the atoms at the leaf nodes of $ T $. The redundancy of $A$ means that there exists an atom $B$ in $ $ with $ (A) ( t) (B) ( t)$. Hence, we can replace $A$ by $B$ and still have a minimum-cardinality edge cover of $ ( t)$ from the atoms at the leaf nodes of $ T $. By iterating this process, we can replace all atoms in the minimum-cardinality edge cover by atoms from the body of $ $. We thus end up with a minimum-cardinality edge cover of $ ( t)$ from the atoms at the leaf nodes of $ T $, which also realizes the edge-cover width of $q_ $ in~$ $.

[Proof of thm:minWidth ] Let $q_ $ be an adorned IDB predicate in $ '$ that realizes the edge-cover width of $q$ in $ '$, i.e., $ _ ' (q) = _ ' (q_ )$. Moreover, let rule $R'$ be a rule in $ '$ with head atom $q_ ( t)$. By Lemma~ [ref] , $q( t)$ has a generalized proof tree $ T $ in $ '$. We define the ``canonical database'' of $q( t)$ w.r.t.\ $ T $ as the EDB $D$ consisting of the following atoms: we start off with the EDB atoms at the leaf nodes of $ T $, but we replace every variable $x_i$ occurring in any atom at the leaf nodes of $ T $ by a distinctive constant $a_i$. We can then turn the generalized proof tree of $q( t)$ into a (standard) proof tree of $q_ (σ( t))$ over the EDB $D$ by applying the substitution $σ$ to all variables occurring in $ T $. Of course, also the rule $ $ fires with substitution $σ$ over the EDB $D$ and produces the IDB atom $q_ (σ( t))$. Now let $\ x_1, , x_m\ $ denote the variables in $ ( t)$ and let $k = _ ' (q)$. This means that the minimum number of body atoms in $ $ and, by Corollary~ [ref] , also the minimum number of atoms from the leaf nodes of $ T $ to cover all of $ ( t)$ is $k$. Likewise, the minimum number of atoms from $D$ to cover all constants $\ a_1, , a_m\ $ is $k$. Now consider another EDB-bounded program $ ''$ of $ $. We want to show that $ _ '' (q) ≥ k$. Suppose to the contrary that $ _ '' (q) < k$. By the definition of EDB-boundedness, $ ''$ contains a rule $R''$ with head predicate $q_ '' $, such that $σ( t)$ is in the IDB relation $q_ '' $. Hence, $ ''$ fires on the EDB $D$ and produces the IDB atom $q(σ( t))$. But then also the rule $ ^*$ obtained from $ ''$ by deleting all body atoms except for a minimum-cardinality edge cover fires on $D$ and produces the IDB atom $q(σ( t))$. But this means that matching the body of $ ^*$ (which consists of less than $k$ atoms) into the EDB $D$ produces less than $k$ atoms of $D$ that cover all constants $\ a_1, , a_m\ $. This contradicts the above observation that at least $k$ atoms from $D$ are required to cover all constants $\ a_1, , a_m\ $.
